name: Philly Roast Pork Sandwich

ingredients.name: skinless boneless pork butt, preferably with fat cap
jarred Italian long hot peppers, other pickled spicy peppers

instructions.primary_message: Mince the garlic. Pick the rosemary leaves from the stems and mince them. Pick the thyme leaves from the stems and mince them. Halve and thinly slice the yellow onion. Trim and cut the broccoli rabe into 1-inch pieces. Mince the garlic. Chop the jarred Italian long hot peppers.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium cloves garlic
1 tbsp fresh rosemary
1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
1 medium yellow onion
1 ¼ lb broccoli rabe
2 medium cloves garlic
¼ cup jarred Italian long hot peppers, other pickled spicy peppers

instructions.primary_message: For the Pork: In a bowl, combine garlic, salt, rosemary, thyme, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. If needed, use a sharp knife to trim fat cap on pork to 1/4 inch, then cut a 1-inch crosshatch pattern in fat cap.

Place pork on a large double layer of plastic wrap. Sprinkle pork all over with salt mixture. Tie pork with kitchen twine at 1-inch intervals, then wrap pork tightly in plastic, place on a platter, and refrigerate for at least 12 hours and up to 24 hours.

Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 325°F. In a large Dutch oven, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add onion and cook until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat.

Unwrap pork and transfer to Dutch oven, fat side up. Add stock, then cover, transfer to oven, and cook until meat registers 180°F in center, 2 to 2 1/2 hours. Remove from the oven and transfer the roast to a carving board, then let cool to room temperature, about 1 hour (if time allows, refrigerate the roast whole until well chilled, at least 2 hours and up to 1 day). Set pork jus aside or refrigerate until ready to use.
For the Sandwiches: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 400℉ (200°C). Remove the kitchen twine from the roast and slice the roast against the grain as thin as possible; set aside.

Reheat the jus over medium-high heat until just simmering, and season with salt to taste. Add the sliced pork with any accumulated juices and mix to coat. Gently simmer until pork is heated through, about 1 minute. Keep warm until ready to assemble sandwiches.

In a 12-inch skillet, heat oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add broccoli rabe, salt, and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned, 6 to 9 minutes. Stir in garlic and pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Stir in peppers and 1 cup of the pork jus from the Dutch oven, bring to a simmer, and cook until liquid is reduced and rabe is very tender, about 5 minutes.

Arrange rolls, split side up, on rimmed baking sheet. Divide provolone evenly among rolls, then bake until cheese is melted and rolls are beginning to toast around the edges, about 3 minutes. Using tongs, divide pork and broccoli rabe evenly among rolls, then ladle a few spoonfuls of remaining jus over each sandwich. Serve.

description: Bursting at the seams with thin slices of succulent pork shoulder, garlicky broccoli rabe, sharp provolone cheese, and finished with a ladle of savory jus, this Philly roast pork sandwich is the real deal.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 16 hr 20 min to 1 day 4 hr 20 min.

Optional substitutions: seeded Italian long rolls → a sturdy Italian hoagie/sub rolls
author: Leah Colins
